preconditions.description: The number of users n is an integer between 2 and 250,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(T1_edges) == n - 1 and len(T2_edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in T1_edges) and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in T2_edges)
preconditions.description: T1_edges and T2_edges are lists of exactly n-1 edges each, where each edge is a pair of integers between 1 and n inclusive, representing the edges of trees T1 and T2 respectively.
Both T1_edges and T2_edges form valid trees on n nodes, where is_tree(edges, n) checks if edges form a connected acyclic graph on n nodes.

postconditions.expression: m == len(matched_pairs) and all(0 <= m < n)
postconditions.description: m is the count of matched edge pairs, where each pair consists of one edge from T1 and one from T2, and m is strictly less than n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and 1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs) and all((a, b) in T1_edges and (c, d) in T2_edges for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: Each matched pair (a, b, c, d) contains valid edges from T1 and T2, where (a, b) is in T1_edges and (c, d) is in T2_edges.

postconditions.expression: all((a, b) != (c, d) for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs) and all((a, b) != (a', b') for (a, b, c, d) in matched_pairs for (a', b', c', d') in matched_pairs if (a, b) != (a', b')) and all((c, d) != (c', d') for (a, b, c, d) in matched_pairs for (a', b', c', d') in matched_pairs if (c, d) != (c'))
postconditions.description: All edges in T1 and T2 are used at most once in the matched_pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected(T1_edges - {(a, b)}, T2_edges + {(c, d)}) for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: For each matched pair (a, b, c, d), removing (a, b) from T1 and adding (c, d) from T2 results in a connected graph, where is_connected(edges, n) checks if the graph formed by edges is connected on n nodes.
m is the size of a maximum matching in the bipartite graph where edges connect (e, f) if T1 - {e} + {f} is connected, and max_matching_size(T1_edges, T2_edges, n) computes this maximum matching size.
